newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL secondaries end lower, blue chips rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL secondaries end lower, blue chips rebound.

text.p: Buying fever in small capitalisation stocks cooled, with the Second Board posting losses at the close for the first time in a week.

But the limpid blue chip sector revived, helped by money switching out of speculative shares and renewed institutional interest, dealers said. A 74-point surge in the Dow overnight also supported sentiment.

The blue chip-centered Composite Index ended up 7.47 points to 1,111.75, and the Second Board slipped 5.44 points or 0.97 percent to 555.55. The smaller capitalisation index had risen to a new intra-day high of 566.41 points earlier today.
"It's as expected," said William Chan, an institutional dealer with Seagroatt and Campbell. "A lot of the main board counters are trading at their lows for the year."

Tony Shue, a vice president in institutional sales at Jupiter Securities, said he had heard of a large firm doing a buy program in Malaysia stocks today. In addition, the market was "getting buy orders out of London."
An institutional dealer with a foreign firm said, "The Second Board is way overstretched, even with wonderful stories."
